title: Attention Conductor: layerwise stochastic gating and microbatch annealer to stabilize FlashAttention v2/v3 rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem summary: Recent FA3 rollouts show intermittent tail-latency spikes and sporadic OOMs on mixed-precision quantized models during cold-starts and prefill-heavy workloads. Existing fallback logic is conservative (global per-model heuristics) and causes quality/cost regressions. Goal: implement a runtime component ("Attention Conductor") that coordinates per-layer kernel choice between FlashAttention v2 and v3, using stochastic gating informed by layer-level microbenchmarks and a microbatch annealing prefill schedule to reduce startup jitter while preserving throughput and avoiding OOMs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No >=3x tail-latency regression vs baseline during cold-start for 95th percentile across representative workloads. 2) OOM rate under 0.01% on QA-scale traces. 3) End-to-end token throughput maintained within -10% of current production baseline for large-context decoding. 4) Observability: per-layer kernel decisions and a small set of new telemetry metrics (layer_choice, probe_latency, annealer_phase) ingested to console dashboards.
implementation_plan: 1) Add lightweight per-layer profiler that runs short synthetic probes for shapes/precision to collect latency and workspace footprint. 2) Implement stochastic gating policy that picks FA2/FA3 with probability tuned from probe results and recent success history. 3) Build microbatch annealer controlling prefill->decode transition: starts aggressive (small microbatches), gradually increases to target to amortize kernel warmup. 4) Integrate graceful fallback: immediate local fallback if probe indicates OOM risk; after N failures auto-force FA2 for layer until next probe. 5) Integrate telemetry hooks and feature flag gated rollout with canary selector by region/instance type.
test_plan: Unit tests for gating logic and annealer state machine. Multi-node QA runs with a curated suite: chat-short, chat-long, long-context summarization, and AMP-quantized T5-family traces. Stress tests for memory pressure and high-concurrency prefill patterns. Canary rollout to 5% of instances in region-us-west1 with comparison dashboards for latency, OOMs, and token throughput. Benchmarks: record 95/99/mean latencies and workspace allocations per layer.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout with instant kill switch. If canary shows >20% regression in P95 or >10x increase in OOMs, revert to global per-model kernel selector and disable annealer for that pool. Postmortem and tuned thresholds before next attempt.
risks: Incorrect probe timings leading to miscalibrated probabilities
Annealer schedule too aggressive causing memory blowouts on heterogeneous GPUs
Telemetry volume from per-layer probes increasing ingestion costs
Edge cases for models with heavy head-slicing or non-standard attention shapes
notes: This approach prioritizes runtime stability and graceful degradation over maximal microbench throughput. We expect some short-term throughput loss on a tiny fraction of workloads in exchange for fewer hard OOMs and less rollout churn. Design reviewed with Research/Applied ML on 2025-02-25. Evaluate whether to persist per-model learned policies to avoid repeated probing for frequently used models.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Ava Chen: Spiked a prototype of per-layer probe harness on dev-gpu1. Observed FA3 faster for head layers but higher workspace for middle layers on 16k context. Saved traces to s3://redwood/inference/attn-conductor/probes/2025-02-21/

2025-02-24 - Marcus Patel: Built initial stochastic gating POC. Gate probability derived from softmax over latency and inverse(workspace) with temperature hyperparam. Early tests show reduced oscillation vs hard thresholding.

2025-02-25 - Design review: Presenters - Marcus, Priya (Applied ML). Feedback: persist per-model decisions and incorporate recent failure history into gate smoothing. Action: add short TTL storage for model-layer policy (24h) in local cache.

2025-02-28 - QA: Canary test run 1 (10%): P95 latency stable, but two OOMs on amp-quantized llama-variant during prefill. Reproduced in bench; root cause appears to be workspace underestimation for interleaved rotary embeddings. Plan: add additional safety margin to workspace estimate for rotary or unusual rotary strides.
2025-03-03 - Marcus: Implemented annealer with 3 phases (probe, ramp, steady). Ramp uses exponentially growing microbatch factor across first 8 decode steps. Updated telemetry labels: annealer_phase.
2025-03-04 - Infra: PR #8421 created for telemetry ingestion changes and dashboard panels. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421

2025-03-05 - Marcus: Running extended 24h canary in us-west1 with persistent model-policy cache. Observed 0 OOMs in canary window and P95 within 6% of baseline. Still collecting more samples for quota-sensitive workloads. Next: expand to additional GPU types for cross-arch validation.
